idea-plugin.name: Claude Code Chat
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code for JetBrains IDE

Bring the full power of Claude Code directly into your IDE. Chat with Claude in a side panel, edit code inline with natural-language instructions, fix errors with one click in the Alt+Enter menu, generate commit messages from your staged diff, and let Claude read, edit, and create files in your project — all without leaving IntelliJ or your favorite IDE.

Inline AI Actions

  • Edit with Claude (Cmd+Alt+K / Ctrl+Alt+K, or the Claude icon in the floating code toolbar) — select code, describe a change in plain English, review the diff, and accept or reject.
  • Fix with Claude — Alt+Enter on any IDE-detected error or warning to get an AI-powered quick-fix that lives next to IntelliJ's own intentions.
  • Generate Commit Message — one click in the VCS commit dialog turns your staged diff into a Conventional Commits-style message.
  • Apply link on every chat code block — replace the selection in your active editor with the suggested code after a diff review.

Chat Panel

  • Multiple parallel Claude Code sessions in a side panel
  • Project-aware: Claude works in your open project's directory
  • Session memory: Claude remembers context across messages
  • Resume past chats — a clock-icon dropdown in the tool window header lists recent sessions per project. Pick one and the previous conversation auto-loads inline (read straight from Claude's local transcript, no API cost) so you can continue from where you left off after closing the IDE. Inline pencil / trash icons rename or remove entries.
  • Markdown rendering with syntax-highlighted code blocks
  • Tool-use indicators with colored status signals and diff summaries
  • File chips — drag/drop, copy/paste, or type a filename to attach files as context; resolves bare filenames against your project
  • Image paste — paste a screenshot or any clipboard image; saved to a temp PNG and sent to Claude as a multimodal input on submit
  • Large-text paste chips — long pastes collapse into a compact chip; double-click to expand back into the input
  • Queue messages while Claude works — type a follow-up (or /btw <message>) while a response is streaming and it queues instead of being lost, then sends automatically when the turn finishes; remove queued items before they go
  • Smart auto-scroll — follows new output unless you've scrolled up to read; "Jump to latest" button keeps you in control
  • Inline diffs: expandable old vs. new for every edit Claude makes, with consolidated stats per file
  • Clickable file links and a changed-files summary grouped by folder
  • Copy and re-edit buttons on messages and code blocks

Right-Click Context Menu

  • Explain — understand code, methods, files, or entire folders (recursive summaries)
  • Refactor — get suggestions for readability, performance, and best practices
  • Generate Tests — create unit tests for selected code, whole files, or every source file in a folder (14+ languages)
  • Fix — identify and fix bugs in selected code
  • Open Claude Session Here — right-click any folder to start a new session rooted there
  • Debug with Claude — right-click in the Run/Debug console to send exceptions, log flows, or output to Claude

Works from the editor, project tree, and Run/Debug console.

Productivity

  • Auto-updating model catalog — the model dropdown refreshes every 24h from a published list (with bundled offline fallback), so new Claude releases become available without a plugin update. Deprecated models get a (deprecated) badge and a one-click swap to the recommended replacement.
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Cmd+Shift+I to toggle the chat panel, Cmd+Alt+K for inline edit (Ctrl variants on Windows/Linux)
  • Stop requests with Escape
  • Permission mode: Plan (read-only Read/Grep/Glob), Content Only (file writes/edits OK, shell blocked), or Unrestricted (allow all) — maps to the CLI's --permission-mode
  • Project tree auto-refreshes when Claude creates, modifies, or deletes files
  • Cost tracking per response

Settings — Model & inference

  • Extended thinking budget — Off / Low (1k) / Medium (8k) / High (32k). Sets MAX_THINKING_TOKENS for Opus/Sonnet 4.x; other models ignore it. Trade speed and cost for deeper reasoning on harder tasks.
  • Append system prompt — multi-line text appended to Claude's system prompt every spawn via --append-system-prompt. Use for project conventions, preferred tone, persona instructions.
  • Max agentic turns — hard cap on the tool-call loop via --max-turns. 0 = unlimited (CLI default).

MCP Servers

  • MCP server management UI — a server icon in the tool-window header (and a button in Settings) opens a manager that aggregates every MCP server Claude can see for the project: project .mcp.json, plus the user and project-local scopes inside ~/.claude.json. Add, edit, and remove servers across all three scopes.
  • All transports — stdio (command + args + env) and remote SSE / HTTP (URL + headers, optional OAuth client id / callback port).
  • Live status — connection/auth badges (✓ connected, ✗ failed, ⏸ pending approval, 🔒 needs authentication) from a health-checked claude mcp list.
  • Authentication, your way — choose API Key / Token, OAuth, or No Auth per server. OAuth sign-in runs in the background and simply opens your browser to finish (no terminal); Authenticate All walks every server that needs it, one at a time, with a live progress panel (skip/remove, countdown). Your chat sessions then use the servers automatically.
  • All writes go through the claude mcp add-json / remove CLI, so your large, live ~/.claude.json is never hand-edited.

Settings Files Editor

  • Edit Claude Code's settings.json at project, project-local, or global scope — a JSON-file icon in the header (and a Settings button) opens it.
  • Structured or raw — a key/value Form tab adds/edits/removes top-level settings (with common keys suggested and typed JSON values), or switch to the JSON tab for raw edits. Both are validated as a JSON object before saving, and unrelated keys (including the plugin's permission grants) are preserved.

Prerequisites

  • Install the Claude CLI: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code (works on macOS, Linux, and Windows)
  • Authenticate by running claude in a terminal
  • Make sure the CLI is on your PATH so the plugin can spawn it. On Windows, npm typically installs claude.cmd under %APPDATA%\npm\ — that directory must be on PATH.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.2

  • Account sign-in: /login — sign in to (or out of) your Anthropic account right from the chat. /login opens a dialog showing your current account, lets you choose subscription or Console (API billing), opens the browser for OAuth, and takes the authorization code you paste back. Built on claude auth, so it works on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
  • Authenticate All — pre-warmed, near-instant sign-ins — instead of cold-starting a hidden claude for each server in turn, several are now warmed up in the background to the sign-in prompt and parked there, then activated one at a time so each browser opens almost instantly. You pay the cold start once, then sign in to each tab in quick succession. The warm-up pool size is configurable (Settings → MCP Servers) and grows automatically if you sign in faster than servers warm up; Skip / Remove drops a server and tears down its pre-warmed process.
  • Fix: "Authenticate All" no longer gets stuck on "signing in…" with many servers — a completed sign-in is now confirmed with a fast single-server health check (claude mcp get) instead of claude mcp list, which health-checks every configured server and could exceed its timeout on large lists. If a callback is slow to arrive, the flow also re-presses Authenticate once.
  • Clickable links in code — URLs inside fenced code blocks and inline `code` spans are now clickable, not just plain text you had to copy/paste. (Prose URLs were already clickable.)
  • Fix: answering a question no longer fails with "send it manually" — submitting an answer to one of Claude's multiple-choice questions while the asking turn was still finishing could give up instantly. The answer now queues and sends the moment the turn ends.
  • Fix: "Switch to Unrestricted" / Allow now actually retries — granting a permission (or switching mode) after a blocked tool stopped the request but often failed to resend it, because the retry gave up before the process finished stopping. It now waits properly and re-runs your prompt. Reading a file outside the working directory reliably surfaces the grant / Unrestricted choices, including when the denial arrives as structured text blocks.
  • Fix: streaming session resumes correctly — in the experimental streaming mode, resuming a saved chat (or recovering after a restart) now continues the same conversation via --resume instead of silently starting a blank one under a new id.

1.2.1

  • Authenticate All — live progress & faster advancement — a non-modal panel now lists every queued server (waiting / authenticating / done / failed / skipped), shows the current server with a countdown of how long it'll wait, and lets you Skip current or Remove a pending server to avoid the wait. Each server advances the moment it connects: instead of waiting out a timeout while scraping the terminal, the flow polls claude mcp list (the same live health check as Refresh) and proceeds as soon as the server reports connected, then tears down promptly. One stuck or misconfigured server can no longer block the rest.
  • Fix: no false permission prompts in Unrestricted mode — when running Unrestricted (bypass permissions), a failing tool no longer triggers a bogus "blocked by your permission mode" message or an offer to allow the command / switch to a mode you're already in — the real error is shown instead. The permission UI now keys off the session's effective mode (the per-session chip override, not just the global default).
  • Queue messages & /btw — type a follow-up while Claude is working and it now queues (shown above the input, removable) instead of being dropped, then sends automatically when the turn finishes. /btw <message> queues a side message any time. (Each queued message is answered after the current turn — claude -p runs one turn at a time.)
  • Context meter — the status row shows how full the model's context window is (◑ N%, amber ≥75%, red ≥90%, token tooltip), so you know when to start a fresh chat. Resets on /clear.
  • Effort & fallback model — Settings → Model & inference: an Effort level (--effort: Low … Max) and a Fallback model (--fallback-model, used automatically when the primary is overloaded/unavailable).
  • CLAUDE.md memory — /init has Claude analyze the project and write/refresh a CLAUDE.md; /memory (and Settings → "Edit CLAUDE.md…") opens an editor for it at project / local / user scope.
  • Streaming session (experimental) — an opt-in mode (Settings → Debug) that runs one long-lived claude process per chat over streaming I/O instead of one per message — faster turns and groundwork for mid-turn steering. Off by default.
  • In-chat debug log export — the chat's Debug panel now has Export / Clear buttons, and streaming mode logs the same per-event detail as the standard path. Compatible with JetBrains IDEs through 2026.2.

1.2.0

  • Reliable MCP OAuth sign-in — authenticating a remote server now drives an interactive claude in a pseudo-TTY the plugin owns, paced off the screen's actual content (onboarding gates → /mcp → the right server → Authenticate) instead of typing into the IDE terminal on fixed timers. It runs hidden — you just finish in the browser claude opens — and quits claude gracefully so the token is flushed (fixes "the browser said success but it still needs authentication").
  • Authorization type picker — the Add/Edit dialog now has an Authorization selector — No Auth, API Key / Token, or OAuth — and shows only the fields that apply (API token, or OAuth client id / secret / callback port), with Headers available for every type. The type is inferred from the saved config, so it always reflects what's actually stored.
  • OAuth client secret + token auth — confidential OAuth providers (e.g. Google Drive) are supported via a client id + secret (the secret is handed to claude over MCP_CLIENT_SECRET, never written to config); token-based servers (e.g. GitHub) authenticate directly via an Authorization: Bearer header with no browser step.
  • Authenticate All — a one-click action in the MCP manager walks every remote server that needs sign-in, one browser at a time, advancing automatically and reporting an end-of-run summary of what succeeded and what didn't (and why). A per-server watchdog guarantees one misconfigured or stuck server can never block the rest.
  • Clear auth feedback — single and batch attempts now surface a result: ✓ authenticated, or a specific reason (needs an API token, sign-in not completed, menu couldn't be driven) with what to do next. Trying OAuth on a token-only server no longer fails silently.
  • Debug logging + export — an opt-in Debug toggle in Settings records diagnostics (including the MCP auth transcript) to an in-memory buffer; an Export debug log… button (shown only while debug is on) saves it for bug reports. Off by default — nothing is recorded while off.
  • Bug fix: OAuth client id round-trip — a pre-registered OAuth client id / callback port now reloads correctly in the Edit dialog (they're stored nested under oauth in the config, which the reader previously missed).

1.1.0

  • MCP server management UI — a new server icon in the tool-window header (and a Manage MCP Servers… button in Settings) opens a manager that aggregates every MCP server visible to the project: project .mcp.json plus the user and project-local scopes in ~/.claude.json (matched by canonical path, so CLI-added local servers show up). Add, edit, remove and authenticate servers across project / local / user scopes.
  • All transports + live status — stdio (command/args/env) and remote SSE / HTTP (URL/headers, optional OAuth client id + callback port). Connection/auth badges (✓ connected, ✗ failed, ⏸ pending approval, 🔒 needs authentication) come from a health-checked claude mcp list.
  • Authenticate remote MCP servers — for OAuth servers, one click opens an interactive claude terminal and brings up the /mcp screen to sign in; the plugin's -p chat sessions then pick up the stored tokens automatically. (The CLI owns the OAuth browser+callback flow; there is no headless MCP-auth command.)
  • Safe writes — all MCP mutations go through claude mcp add-json / remove rather than hand-editing ~/.claude.json. Using add-json also passes the whole server definition as one JSON argument, sidestepping a variadic-flag pitfall where --header could swallow the URL ("missing required argument 'commandOrUrl'").
  • MCP tool permission grants in chat — when Claude is blocked on an mcp__<server>__<tool> call, the in-chat grant banner now fires and offers the right patterns: allow this exact mcp__server__tool vs allow broad mcp__server (every tool from that server).
  • Settings files editor — a JSON-file icon in the header (and an Edit settings.json… button in Settings) edits Claude Code's own settings.json at project / project-local / global scope, with a structured key/value Form tab and a raw JSON tab. Both are validated as a JSON object before saving; unrelated keys (including the plugin's permission grants in settings.local.json) are preserved.
  • Paste fixes — pasting a URL whose last path segment matches a project filename no longer turns it into a file chip; an absolute path that doesn't exist on disk is no longer silently re-mapped to a same-named project file; and every chip (file chips included) now expands to its underlying text on double-click.

1.0.6

  • Auto-retry on permission grant — clicking "Allow this exact …", "Allow all …", or "Switch to Unrestricted" on a permission-denied banner now stops the in-flight (or already-finished) request, applies the grant, and automatically resends the original prompt with the new permission in place. Previously you had to wait, click Stop, and re-send manually.
  • Failure badges show what actually went wrong — when a tool returns an error, the badge now reads e.g. "✗ failed Bash: java: command not found" instead of a bare "✗ failed". Consecutive failures of the same tool collapse into one line with a "(Nx)" counter so a retrying tool doesn't spam the chat.
  • Plugin version on the Welcome page — the header now reads "Claude Code (v1.0.6)" so it's obvious which build is running. Version is baked in at build time so the plugin no longer touches PluginManagerCore (now @ApiStatus.Internal in 2026.2+ EAP and flagged by the marketplace verifier).
  • Recent chats — a clock-icon dropdown in the tool window header lists past sessions for the current project (kept per-project, capped at 10, 30-day TTL). Click one to reopen the conversation; Claude picks up where it left off via --resume <id>. Each row has inline pencil (rename) and trash (delete) icons; hover highlights the row. Deleting only removes the dropdown entry — Claude's own transcript under ~/.claude/projects is untouched.
  • Full transcript on resume — when you open a recent chat, the previous conversation auto-loads from Claude's local JSONL (no API call, no token cost) and renders inline as proper chat blocks — user bubbles, markdown-rendered assistant replies, code blocks — terminated by an "End of previous history" separator. Reading is free; if the local file is missing, the chat still works (Claude has the conversation server-side).
  • Permission mode auto-applies on resume — whatever permission mode the original session ran with is reapplied as a per-session chip override, so the resumed chat behaves like the original. Global default is untouched.
  • Settings — Model & inference — three new controls:
    • Extended thinking — Off / Low (1k) / Medium (8k) / High (32k). Sets MAX_THINKING_TOKENS on the spawned claude process. Effective on Opus / Sonnet 4.x; other models ignore it.
    • Append system prompt — multi-line text appended to Claude's system prompt every spawn via --append-system-prompt. Use for project conventions, preferred tone, persona instructions.
    • Max agentic turns — spinner cap on the agentic tool-call loop via --max-turns. 0 = unlimited (CLI default).
  • Models catalog with auto-refresh — the model list now updates from a published catalog every 24h (with a bundled offline fallback), so new Claude models become available without a plugin update. Deprecated models render with a (deprecated) suffix and a one-click swap to the recommended replacement when selected. The Refresh catalog button in Settings forces an immediate re-fetch. <synthetic> and similar internal placeholders are filtered out.
  • Settings: model field is no longer free-text — pick from the catalog (or Default for "let Claude Code choose"). Avoids silent typos that produced "exited with code 1" errors. A Clear custom history button wipes the persisted list of model IDs Claude has responded with that aren't in the catalog.
  • Async confirmation dialogs now surface in front of Settings — fix for Refresh catalog where the success notice was appearing behind the modal Settings dialog. Captures the dialog's ModalityState on the EDT and re-uses it on the async callback, so the Messages dialog stacks above.
  • Esc is now the only "stop current request" shortcut — removed the legacy double Cmd+C / Ctrl+C handling everywhere (Welcome page, README, plugin description). Cmd/Ctrl+C in the input area now just copies, never interrupts Claude.

1.0.5

  • Fix-with-Claude intention description added — newer IntelliJ builds require <intentionAction> registrations to ship a description.html plus before/after templates under resources/intentionDescriptions/<ClassName>/. Without them the IDE logged a SEVERE on every load and the intention couldn't appear in the Settings → Editor → Intentions list. Files now included.
  • Plugin-load SEVERE fixed — removed an <add-to-group group-id="Floating.CodeToolbar.Web"> registration that referenced a non-existent action group. Logged a SEVERE error in idea.log on every plugin load (the rest of the plugin still worked). The Edit-with-Claude floating-toolbar registration in Floating.CodeToolbar remains and continues to cover JS/TS via the platform's per-language routing in recent IntelliJ versions.
  • Paste screenshots into the chat — Cmd+V / Ctrl+V (or drag-drop) on a clipboard image now creates an image chip showing the dimensions. The image is saved to a temp PNG and referenced via the CLI's @<path> syntax on submit, so Claude receives it as a multimodal input. Works for screenshots (macOS Cmd+Shift+Ctrl+4, Windows Win+Shift+S), Preview's Edit→Copy, and browser image right-click→Copy.
  • Generate Commit Message: reads selected changes from the dialog — previously the action ran git diff --cached, which could be stale relative to what the user had ticked in the commit dialog (forcing a "refresh" click before generation). Now reads VcsDataKeys.SELECTED_CHANGES directly and diffs exactly those file paths against HEAD; falls back to staged-then-unstaged if no selection is available.
  • Generate Commit Message: better synthesis across multi-file change sets — the prompt now receives a git diff --stat summary alongside the patch, and tells Claude explicitly to find the unifying intent across all files rather than describing the most prominent one.
  • Deprecated API fix — replaced FileChooserDescriptorFactory.createSingleFileDescriptor() with the equivalent FileChooserDescriptor constructor in the Settings → Browse… button. Flagged by the JetBrains plugin verifier; no behaviour change.

1.0.4

  • Windows support — the CLI invocation no longer assumes the Unix script command for pty allocation; on Windows it spawns claude.cmd directly. Mac/Linux behaviour is unchanged. claude resolution layers three strategies because IntelliJ's JVM often inherits a PATH that's missing the user-PATH entries added by the Node.js MSI installer (where %APPDATA%\npm\ normally sits) — meaning a bare claude can be runnable from CMD/PowerShell yet invisible to the plugin: (1) where against the inherited PATH; (2) direct probes of %APPDATA%\npm, %LOCALAPPDATA%\npm, %ProgramFiles%\nodejs; (3) npm config get prefix. Prefers the .cmd extension over the Unix shell-script wrapper that npm also installs. The resolved binary's directory is also prepended to the spawned process's PATH so internal shell-outs from claude.cmd work. Settings → Claude CLI path accepts an absolute path as a manual fallback if auto-detection fails.
  • Permission modes (replaces auto-accept toggle) — Settings → Tools → Claude Code now exposes a permission-mode dropdown: acceptEdits (default, file edits go through, shell commands blocked), bypassPermissions (Claude can run any tool), or plan (read-only). Maps directly to the CLI's --permission-mode. The old binary "auto-accept" toggle pretended an interactive permission flow that the CLI's -p mode doesn't actually support; this replaces it with what the CLI really offers.
  • Permission-blocked hint — when Claude's reply looks like it's been blocked by your current permission mode (e.g. "Could you approve the Write tool…"), an inline hint appears with a clickable link straight to Settings to switch modes.
  • Edit with Claude in the floating toolbar — now for JS/TS too — the JavaScript/TypeScript plugin uses its own Floating.CodeToolbar.Web group separate from the generic one, so the Claude icon was missing on web files. Action now registers to both groups; the keyboard shortcut was unaffected.
  • Deprecated API fix — replaced ReadAction.compute(ThrowableComputable) with Application.runReadAction(Computable) in the chat-input filename resolver. Flagged by the JetBrains plugin verifier as deprecated and slated for removal in a future platform release. No behaviour change.

1.0.3

  • Edit with Claude — select code, hit Cmd+Alt+K / Ctrl+Alt+K (or click the Claude icon in the floating code toolbar, alongside Show Context Actions / Extract / Surround), then type a natural-language instruction. Claude returns the rewrite and a side-by-side diff opens; Accept replaces the selection, Reject discards it. Works in any editor regardless of language.
  • Apply button on chat code blocks — every fenced code block in the Claude chat now has an [apply] link next to [copy]. Select the target code in the active editor, click apply, review the diff, and accept to replace your selection in-place.
  • Generate Commit Message with Claude — new button in the VCS commit dialog toolbar. Reads git diff --cached (falls back to git diff), sends it to Claude, and fills the commit message field with a Conventional Commits-style result.
  • Fix with Claude quick-fix intention — Alt+Enter on any IDE-detected error or warning now offers "Fix with Claude". Sends the offending lines + the inspection message to Claude, shows a diff, applies on accept. Works for any language and any inspection (compiler errors, linter warnings, code-style issues).
  • Expandable paste chips — large-text paste chips can now be double-clicked to expand back into the input. Cursor changes to a pointer and a tooltip reminds you of the gesture; file chips remain non-expandable to keep their path semantics intact.
  • Inline code completion removed — the experimental opt-in was dropped after evaluation: with the CLI-based auth path, latency was 1.5-3s per suggestion vs. sub-200ms for purpose-built FIM models. Will revisit if Anthropic ships a low-latency endpoint.

1.0.2

  • Smart auto-scroll — chat output only follows new messages when you're already at the bottom; if you've scrolled up to read, your position is preserved. A floating "↓ Jump to latest" button appears in the bottom-right when you're scrolled away.
  • File chips in chat input — drag/drop, copy/paste, or paste a path and it becomes a compact 📎 filename chip that expands to the absolute path on submit. Click the ✕ to remove.
  • Smart filename resolution — pasting just a filename (with or without extension) resolves to the project file via FilenameIndex; on macOS, Finder copies are read from NSPasteboard via AppleScript when JBR's clipboard bridge only exposes the bare filename.
  • Large-text paste chips — pasting >250 chars or >3 lines creates a "Pasted #N · X lines" chip instead of cluttering the input. Submitted text uses the full content.
  • Open Claude Session Here — right-click any folder in the project tree to open a new Claude Code session rooted at that folder.
  • Editable model selector — type any model ID in Settings, not just the bundled list; recognized models from sessions are remembered. Adds Opus 4.7 to the bundled list.
  • Better diff summary — Edit results now show ~modified, +added, -removed with proper LCS-based counts instead of overcounting.
  • Tool-aware thinking indicator — shows the running tool name and elapsed seconds while Claude is working.
  • Tool window focus — Send-to-Claude actions now activate the Claude tool window (focusing the input) rather than just showing it.
  • Debug log off by default — checkbox starts unchecked so it doesn't take up space.

1.0.1

  • Explain Folder — right-click any folder in the project tree to get a hierarchical summary of its contents, with breakdowns for each sub-folder up to 2 levels deep
  • File-type agnostic explanations — Explain works on any file type (Dockerfile, YAML, Kubernetes manifests, build files, etc.), not just source code
  • Improved prompts — all right-click action prompts rewritten with structured output format, better guidance for test generation (matches project conventions), and concrete code in refactor/fix results
  • Settings crash fix — fixed a NullPointerException that occurred when opening Settings during plugin unload

1.0.0

  • Console integration — right-click in Run/Debug console to debug exceptions, explain log flows, or send output to Claude
  • Folder-level test generation — generate tests for all source files in a directory (supports 14+ languages)
  • Send to Claude — send selected code, files, or console output as context from any right-click menu
  • Interactive permission prompts — Allow/Deny buttons in the chat panel for Claude's file operations
  • Inline diffs — expandable diff viewers showing old vs. new code for every edit Claude makes
  • Edit consolidation — consecutive edits to the same file are grouped into a single entry with cumulative diffs
  • Thinking display — real-time indicator showing Claude's reasoning when extended thinking is active
  • Debug log panel — collapsible panel for inspecting internal session operations
  • Session auto-naming — sessions are automatically named based on the first message
  • Auto-accept permissions setting — configure whether file operations require manual approval
  • File deletion tracking — detects and displays files deleted via Bash commands
  • Model info in header — active model name shown in each response header

0.1.0

  • Initial release
  • Multi-session chat panel with Claude Code CLI
  • Right-click actions: Explain, Refactor, Generate Tests, Fix
  • Editor and project tree context menu integration
  • Markdown rendering with syntax highlighting
  • Clickable file links and changed files summary
  • Copy/edit buttons on messages and code blocks
  • Model selection and cost tracking
  • Welcome page with feature overview
